speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are an adolescent with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To understand the underlying cause, can you describe exactly what these unusual physical features look like, such as specific facial characteristics or skeletal abnormalities?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency) with 46,XY DSD (female external phenotype).

The findings of ambiguous genitalia (partial labial fusion, clitoromegaly) at birth, combined with virilization in the mother (hirsutism) and the patient (severe acne, bone fragility likely due to Cushingoid effects), strongly suggest a genetic form of CAH. REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone; REQUEST TEST: Karyotype; REQUEST TEST: Renal function and electrolytes.
